```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Package specification – unchanged
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE CreatingDataBase IS
    PROCEDURE Filling;
    PROCEDURE Deleting;
END CreatingDataBase;
/
 
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Package body – added a private helper to write the log
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY CreatingDataBase IS

    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- Private helper: write an exception to PACKAGE_ERRORS
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    PROCEDURE log_error(p_proc_name VARCHAR2) IS
    BEGIN
        INSERT INTO PACKAGE_ERRORS (
            PROC_NAME,
            ERR_CODE,
            ERR_MSG,
            ERR_LINE
        )
        VALUES (
            p_proc_name,
            SQLCODE,
            DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK,
            DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE
        );
        /* No explicit COMMIT – the caller (or Scheduler) will
           commit/rollback the whole transaction.  If you want the
           log to survive a later rollback you could make this
           procedure AUTONOMOUS TRANSACTION, but for a simple demo
           the default behaviour is fine. */
    EXCEPTION
        WHEN OTHERS THEN
            /* If logging itself fails we don't want an infinite loop.
               Write to the alert log instead. */
            DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('*** Logging failed: '||SQLERRM);
    END log_error;
    
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- Procedure: Filling
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    PROCEDURE Filling IS
    BEGIN
        /* ---- INSERT demo data ---- */
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (FIRM_ID, FIRM_NAME) VALUES (1, 'Apple');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (FIRM_ID, FIRM_NAME) VALUES (2, 'HP');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (FIRM_ID, FIRM_NAME) VALUES (3, 'Dell');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (FIRM_ID, FIRM_NAME) VALUES (4, 'Lenovo');

        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (TYPE_ID, TYPE_NAME) VALUES (1, 'Laptop');
        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (TYPE_ID, TYPE_NAME) VALUES (2, 'Desktop');
        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (TYPE_ID, TYPE_NAME) VALUES (3, 'Tablet');

        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (COMPUTER_ID, FREQUENCY, TYPE_ID, FIRM_ID)
        VALUES (1, 2100, 1, 1);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (COMPUTER_ID, FREQUENCY, TYPE_ID, FIRM_ID)
        VALUES (2, 2600, 2, 2);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (COMPUTER_ID, FREQUENCY, TYPE_ID, FIRM_ID)
        VALUES (3, 2400, 1, 3);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (COMPUTER_ID, FREQUENCY, TYPE_ID, FIRM_ID)
        VALUES (4, 1800, 3, 4);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (COMPUTER_ID, FREQUENCY, TYPE_ID, FIRM_ID)
        VALUES (5, 2000, 1, 2);

        COMMIT;   -- make the rows visible to other sessions
    EXCEPTION
        WHEN OTHERS THEN
            log_error('Filling');
            RAISE;   -- re‑raise so the Scheduler (or caller) knows it failed
    END Filling;
    
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- Procedure: Deleting
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    PROCEDURE Deleting IS
    BEGIN
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE COMPUTERS';
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE COMPUTER_TYPES';
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE FIRMS';
        /* TRUNCATE does an implicit COMMIT */

            log_error('Deleting');
            RAISE;
    END Deleting;
```

## 4️⃣  Scheduler – run the procedures automatically

Oracle Scheduler (`DBMS_SCHEDULER`) is the modern way to run PL/SQL code at set times.  
Below are two example jobs:

* **Nightly fill** – runs every night at 02:00 AM.
* **Weekly clean‑up** – runs every Sunday at 03:30 AM.

```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   1️⃣  Create a Scheduler program (optional – makes reuse easy)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
BEGIN
    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_PROGRAM(
        program_name   => 'PROC_FILLING',
        program_type   => 'STORED_PROCEDURE',
        program_action => 'CreatingDataBase.Filling',
        enabled        => TRUE,
        comments       => 'Calls the Filling procedure'
    );

    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_PROGRAM(
        program_name   => 'PROC_DELETING',
        program_type   => 'STORED_PROCEDURE',
        program_action => 'CreatingDataBase.Deleting',
        enabled        => TRUE,
        comments       => 'Calls the Deleting procedure'
    );
END;
/
 
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   2️⃣  Create the two jobs
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
BEGIN
    /* Nightly fill – every day at 02:00 */
    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
        job_name        => 'JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY',
        program_name    => 'PROC_FILLING',
        start_date      => SYSTIMESTAMP,
        repeat_interval => 'FREQ=DAILY; BYHOUR=2; BYMINUTE=0; BYSECOND=0',
        enabled         => TRUE,
        auto_drop       => FALSE,
        comments        => 'Populate demo tables each night'
    );

    /* Weekly clean‑up – every Sunday at 03:30 */
    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
        job_name        => 'JOB_DELETING_WEEKLY',
        program_name    => 'PROC_DELETING',
        start_date      => SYSTIMESTAMP,
        repeat_interval => 'FREQ=WEEKLY; BYDAY=SUN; BYHOUR=3; BYMINUTE=30; BYSECOND=0',
        enabled         => TRUE,
        auto_drop       => FALSE,
        comments        => 'Truncate demo tables each week'
    );
END;
/
 
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   3️⃣  (Optional) View the jobs
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT job_name,
       enabled,
       state,
       last_start_date,
       next_run_date
FROM   user_scheduler_jobs
ORDER  BY job_name;
```

### How to control the jobs

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| **Disable** a job (e.g., while you are testing) | `BEGIN DBMS_SCHEDULER.DISABLE('JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY'); END; /` |
| **Enable** again | `BEGIN DBMS_SCHEDULER.ENABLE('JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY'); END; /` |
| **Run now** (manual trigger) | `BEGIN DBMS_SCHEDULER.RUN_JOB('JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY'); END; /` |
| **Check last run status** | `SELECT * FROM user_scheduler_job_run_details WHERE job_name='JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY' ORDER BY log_date DESC;` |

All of this can be executed once (e.g., from SQL*Developer, SQL*Plus, or any SQL client). After that the Scheduler will take care of the timing – you don’t need to open a console each night.

## 1️⃣  Email alerts from `log_error`

**Prerequisite** – `UTL_MAIL` must be installed and the SMTP server configured in the database (`UTL_MAIL.SMTP_HOST`).  
If you are on an Oracle 11g R2+ or 12c+ database the package is usually already present; you only need the ACL (see the *Permissions* section below).

### Updated `log_error` procedure

```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Inside the package body – replace the previous log_error
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
PROCEDURE log_error(p_proc_name VARCHAR2) IS
    l_subject  VARCHAR2(200);
    l_body     VARCHAR2(4000);
BEGIN
    /* 1️⃣  Insert the row in the logging table */
    INSERT INTO PACKAGE_ERRORS (
        PROC_NAME,
        ERR_CODE,
        ERR_MSG,
        ERR_LINE
    )
    VALUES (
        p_proc_name,
        SQLCODE,
        DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK,
        DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE
    );

    /* 2️⃣  Build a tiny e‑mail */
    l_subject := 'Oracle Package Error – '||p_proc_name;
    l_body    := 'Procedure : '||p_proc_name||CHR(10)||
                 'Error code: '||SQLCODE||CHR(10)||
                 'Message   : '||DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK||CHR(10)||
                 'Backtrace : '||DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE||CHR(10)||
                 'Logged at : '||SYSTIMESTAMP;

    /* 3️⃣  Send it – UTL_MAIL requires the ACL to allow SMTP */
    UTL_MAIL.SEND(
        sender      => 'oracle@yourcompany.com',   -- change to a valid address
        recipients  => 'you@example.com',          -- who should receive the alert
        subject     => l_subject,
        message     => l_body,
        mime_type   => 'text/plain; charset=us-ascii'
    );
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        /* If the e‑mail itself fails we do not want to loop forever.
           Write a short note to the alert log instead. */
        DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('*** log_error: email failed – '||SQLERRM);
END log_error;
```

*If you prefer **APEX_MAIL** (available only inside an APEX workspace) replace the `UTL_MAIL.SEND` block with:*

```sql
APEX_MAIL.SEND(
    p_to        => 'you@example.com',
    p_from      => 'oracle@yourcompany.com',
    p_subject   => l_subject,
    p_body      => l_body );
APEX_MAIL.PUSH_QUEUE;   -- forces immediate delivery
```

## 2️⃣  Quick view of Scheduler job history

```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   Shows the last 20 runs of the two jobs you created.
   Columns: job name, status, start‑time, end‑time, run‑duration,
            any error message (if failed)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT job_name,
       status,
       TO_CHAR(start_date,      'YYYY‑MM‑DD HH24:MI:SS') AS started_at,
       TO_CHAR(end_date,        'YYYY‑MM‑DD HH24:MI:SS') AS finished_at,
       ROUND( (end_date - start_date)*24*60, 2)      AS run_minutes,
       CASE
         WHEN status = 'FAILED' THEN error# || ': ' || error_msg
         ELSE NULL
       END                                          AS error_detail
FROM   user_scheduler_job_run_details
WHERE  job_name IN ('JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY','JOB_DELETING_WEEKLY')
ORDER  BY start_date DESC
FETCH  FIRST 20 ROWS ONLY;
```

## 3️⃣  Audit column (`last_modified`) + trigger for each demo table

You only have to run the script **once** (after the tables exist).  
If you later add more tables you can reuse the same pattern.

```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   1️⃣  Add the column (if it does not already exist)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
ALTER TABLE FIRMS          ADD (last_modified TIMESTAMP);
ALTER TABLE COMPUTER_TYPES ADD (last_modified TIMESTAMP);
ALTER TABLE COMPUTERS      ADD (last_modified TIMESTAMP);

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   2️⃣  Create a generic BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger
       that sets last_modified = SYSTIMESTAMP.
       The same code is duplicated for each table – you could
       also use a single BEFORE EACH ROW ON ALL TABLES trigger
       (requires 12c+ and DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB) but the
       explicit version is easier to read.
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_firms_audit
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON FIRMS
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    :NEW.last_modified := SYSTIMESTAMP;
END;
/
 
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_computer_types_audit
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON COMPUTER_TYPES
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    :NEW.last_modified := SYSTIMESTAMP;
END;
/
 
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_computers_audit
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON COMPUTERS
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    :NEW.last_modified := SYSTIMESTAMP;
END;
/
```

*Result:* every `INSERT` or `UPDATE` on those tables automatically stamps the row with the current timestamp. No extra code is needed in your package.

## 4️⃣  Required privileges (what to ask the DBA)

| Feature | Minimal privilege(s) | How to grant (run by a DBA) |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Scheduler jobs** – to run PL/SQL stored procedures and DDL (`TRUNCATE`) | `CREATE JOB` (or `CREATE ANY JOB` if you want to create jobs in other schemas) <br> `EXECUTE` on the package (granted automatically to its owner) | ```sql GRANT CREATE JOB TO <your_schema>; ``` |
| **UTL_MAIL** – to send e‑mail via the database | `EXECUTE` on `UTL_MAIL` <br> Network ACL that permits the schema to connect to the SMTP host on port 25 (or 587) | ```sql BEGIN DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN.CREATE_ACL( acl => 'mail_acl.xml', description => 'Allow SMTP', principal => '<your_schema>', is_grant => TRUE, privilege => 'connect' ); END; /  -- then:  DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN.ADD_PRIVILEGE(acl => 'mail_acl.xml', principal => '<your_schema>', is_grant => TRUE, privilege => 'connect'); DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN.ASSIGN_ACL(acl => 'mail_acl.xml', host => 'smtp.yourcompany.com', lower_port => 25, upper_port => 25); COMMIT; ``` |
| **TRUNCATE** (DDL) inside a stored procedure | `DROP ANY TABLE` is *not* required – the owner of the tables can truncate them. The schema that owns the tables must simply have the `DROP` privilege on its own objects (implicit). If the Scheduler job runs under a **different** schema, grant `DROP ANY TABLE` (or better, create the job with the same owner as the tables). | ```sql GRANT DROP ANY TABLE TO <schema_running_job>; ``` (use with caution) |
| **Access to the logging table** (INSERT) | `INSERT` on `PACKAGE_ERRORS` (granted automatically to the owner) | If another schema will call the package, grant `EXECUTE` on the package and `INSERT` on the table: `GRANT EXECUTE ON CreatingDataBase TO other_schema; GRANT INSERT ON PACKAGE_ERRORS TO other_schema;` |
| **APEX_MAIL** (if you decide to use it) | `EXECUTE` on `APEX_MAIL` and the same ACL as above (APEX_MAIL uses the same network ACL) | `GRANT EXECUTE ON APEX_MAIL TO <your_schema>;` |

> **Tip:** The DBA can verify the ACL with  
> `SELECT * FROM DBA_NETWORK_ACLS;`  
> and can view the job definitions with  
> `SELECT * FROM DBA_SCHEDULER_JOBS WHERE OWNER = USER;`

## Putting it all together – a single “install” script

You can copy‑paste the whole block below (in the order shown) into SQL*Plus, SQL Developer, or any SQL client.  
Only the **email addresses** and **SMTP host** need to be edited for your environment.

```sql
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   0️⃣  (Optional) Clean‑up old objects – run only if you are
        re‑creating everything from scratch.
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
DROP PACKAGE CreatingDataBase   CASCADE;
DROP TABLE PACKAGE_ERRORS;
DROP TRIGGER trg_firms_audit;
DROP TRIGGER trg_computer_types_audit;
DROP TRIGGER trg_computers_audit;
DROP TABLE FIRMS;
DROP TABLE COMPUTER_TYPES;
DROP TABLE COMPUTERS;
-- (Scheduler jobs will be dropped automatically when the package is dropped)

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   1️⃣  Demo tables
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE TABLE FIRMS (
    firm_id   NUMBER PRIMARY KEY,
    firm_name VARCHAR2(30),
    last_modified TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE COMPUTER_TYPES (
    type_id   NUMBER PRIMARY KEY,
    type_name VARCHAR2(30),
    last_modified TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE COMPUTERS (
    computer_id NUMBER PRIMARY KEY,
    frequency   NUMBER,
    type_id     NUMBER REFERENCES COMPUTER_TYPES(type_id),
    firm_id     NUMBER REFERENCES FIRMS(firm_id),
    last_modified TIMESTAMP
);

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   2️⃣  Logging table
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE TABLE PACKAGE_ERRORS (
    log_id     NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    proc_name  VARCHAR2(30),
    err_code   NUMBER,
    err_msg    VARCHAR2(4000),
    err_line   VARCHAR2(4000),
    logged_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT SYSTIMESTAMP
);

/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   3️⃣  Package (with email in log_error)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE CreatingDataBase IS
    PROCEDURE Filling;
    PROCEDURE Deleting;
END CreatingDataBase;
/

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY CreatingDataBase IS

    /* ---------- private helper that logs AND e‑mails ---------- */
    PROCEDURE log_error(p_proc_name VARCHAR2) IS
        l_subject VARCHAR2(200);
        l_body    VARCHAR2(4000);
    BEGIN
        INSERT INTO PACKAGE_ERRORS (
            PROC_NAME,
            ERR_CODE,
            ERR_MSG,
            ERR_LINE
        ) VALUES (
            p_proc_name,
            SQLCODE,
            DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK,
            DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE
        );

        l_subject := 'Oracle Package Error – '||p_proc_name;
        l_body    := 'Procedure : '||p_proc_name||CHR(10)||
                     'Error code: '||SQLCODE||CHR(10)||
                     'Message   : '||DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK||CHR(10)||
                     'Backtrace : '||DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE||CHR(10)||
                     'Logged at : '||SYSTIMESTAMP;

        UTL_MAIL.SEND(
            sender      => 'oracle@yourcompany.com',   -- change
            recipients  => 'you@example.com',          -- change
            subject     => l_subject,
            message     => l_body,
            mime_type   => 'text/plain; charset=us-ascii'
        );
    EXCEPTION
        WHEN OTHERS THEN
            DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('*** log_error: email failed – '||SQLERRM);
    END log_error;

    /* ---------- Filling procedure ---------- */
    PROCEDURE Filling IS
    BEGIN
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (firm_id, firm_name) VALUES (1, 'Apple');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (firm_id, firm_name) VALUES (2, 'HP');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (firm_id, firm_name) VALUES (3, 'Dell');
        INSERT INTO FIRMS (firm_id, firm_name) VALUES (4, 'Lenovo');

        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (type_id, type_name) VALUES (1, 'Laptop');
        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (type_id, type_name) VALUES (2, 'Desktop');
        INSERT INTO COMPUTER_TYPES (type_id, type_name) VALUES (3, 'Tablet');

        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (computer_id, frequency, type_id, firm_id)
        VALUES (1, 2100, 1, 1);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (computer_id, frequency, type_id, firm_id)
        VALUES (2, 2600, 2, 2);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (computer_id, frequency, type_id, firm_id)
        VALUES (3, 2400, 1, 3);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (computer_id, frequency, type_id, firm_id)
        VALUES (4, 1800, 3, 4);
        INSERT INTO COMPUTERS (computer_id, frequency, type_id, firm_id)
        VALUES (5, 2000, 1, 2);

        COMMIT;
    EXCEPTION
        WHEN OTHERS THEN
            log_error('Filling');
            RAISE;
    END Filling;

    /* ---------- Deleting procedure ---------- */
    PROCEDURE Deleting IS
    BEGIN
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE COMPUTERS';
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE COMPUTER_TYPES';
        EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'TRUNCATE TABLE FIRMS';
    EXCEPTION
        WHEN OTHERS THEN
            log_error('Deleting');
            RAISE;
    END Deleting;

END CreatingDataBase;
/
 
/* -------------------------------------------------------------
   4️⃣  Scheduler jobs (run once)
   ------------------------------------------------------------- */
BEGIN
    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_PROGRAM(
        program_name   => 'PROC_FILLING',
        program_type   => 'STORED_PROCEDURE',
        program_action => 'CreatingDataBase.Filling',
        enabled        => TRUE );

    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_PROGRAM(
        program_name   => 'PROC_DELETING',
        program_type   => 'STORED_PROCEDURE',
        program_action => 'CreatingDataBase.Deleting',
        enabled        => TRUE );

    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
        job_name        => 'JOB_FILLING_NIGHTLY',
        program_name    => 'PROC_FILLING',
        start_date      => SYSTIMESTAMP,
        repeat_interval => 'FREQ=DAILY; BYHOUR=2; BYMINUTE=0; BYSECOND=0',
        enabled         => TRUE,
        auto_drop       => FALSE );

    DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
        job_name        => 'JOB_DELETING_WEEKLY',
        program_name    => 'PROC_DELETING',
        start_date      => SYSTIMESTAMP,
        repeat_interval => 'FREQ=WEEKLY; BYDAY=SUN; BYHOUR=3; BYMINUTE=30; BYSECOND=0',
        enabled         => TRUE,
        auto_drop       => FALSE );
END;
/
```

**Graph**  

\(G\) is the 4‑cycle  

\[
1\!-\!2\!-\!3\!-\!4\!-\!1 .
\]

The vertex ordering we use is \((1,2,3,4)\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Adjacency matrix \(A\)

\(A_{ij}=1\) iff \(\{i,j\}\) is an edge, otherwise \(0\).

\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 1 & 0 & 1\\[2pt]
1 & 0 & 1 & 0\\[2pt]
0 & 1 & 0 & 1\\[2pt]
1 & 0 & 1 & 0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors  

We solve \(\det(\lambda I-A)=0\).

\[
\lambda I-A=
\begin{pmatrix}
\lambda & -1 & 0 & -1\\
-1 & \lambda & -1 & 0\\
0 & -1 & \lambda & -1\\
-1 & 0 & -1 & \lambda
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Because the matrix is *circulant* (each row is a cyclic shift of the first), its eigenvalues are known explicitly:

\[
\lambda_k = 2\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{2\pi k}{4}\Bigr),\qquad k=0,1,2,3 .
\]

Evaluating:

\[
\begin{aligned}
k=0 &: \lambda_0 = 2\cos 0 = 2,\\
k=1 &: \lambda_1 = 2\cos \frac{\pi}{2}=0,\\
k=2 &: \lambda_2 = 2\cos \pi = -2,\\
k=3 &: \lambda_3 = 2\cos \frac{3\pi}{2}=0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence the characteristic polynomial is  

\[
\det(\lambda I-A)=\lambda^{2}(\lambda^{2}-4)=0 .
\]

---

#### Eigenvectors (one convenient orthonormal set)

| eigenvalue \(\lambda\) | eigenvector \(v\) (unnormalised) | comment |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------|---------|
| \(2\) | \((1,\,1,\,1,\,1)^{\!\top}\) | constant vector – all entries equal |
| \(-2\) | \((1,\,-1,\,1,\,-1)^{\!\top}\) | alternates sign every step |
| \(0\) (first) | \((1,\,0,\,-1,\,0)^{\!\top}\) | orthogonal to the two above |
| \(0\) (second) | \((0,\,1,\,0,\,-1)^{\!\top}\) | orthogonal to the other three |

You can verify, e.g. for \(\lambda=2\):

\[
A\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2\\2\\2\\2\end{pmatrix}=2\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Similarly \(A(1,-1,1,-1)^{\!\top}= -2(1,-1,1,-1)^{\!\top}\) and \(A\) sends each of the two zero‑vectors to the zero vector.

If you prefer *unit* eigenvectors, just divide each by its Euclidean norm \(\|v\|=\sqrt{4}=2\) (for the first two) or \(\sqrt{2}\) (for the zero‑eigenvectors).

The **spectrum** is the multiset of all eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity:

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(G)=\{\,2,\;0,\;0,\;-2\,\}} .
\]
